# Task map {#sec-appg}

Use this map to look for a task phrased as "How do I ...?", rather than a topic name. A task entry should lead
to the section that supplies the answer or state why the answer is not provided. Read the status and the
destination together: a link alone does not establish that the task is documented completely.

The status describes the book's answer to the particular task. It is not a test result or a statement that
every related operation works in every configuration.

| status | how to interpret it |
|---|---|
| answered | Read the answering section for the documented task and its conditions. |
| partly documented | Read the available answer and the stated missing part before using it. |
| undocumented | The book does not supply the required answer; this does not imply unsupported code. |
| unsupported by the code | The requested operation is identified as unsupported; read the reason and its scope. |
| outside scope | The task lies outside the book's stated scope, independently of implementation support. |

: Reading the task-status labels. {#tbl-appg-status-guide}

For an entry with a destination, follow the answering section rather than stopping at a chapter overview.
Check that the section describes the inputs, options, expected output and failure conditions needed for your
task. For a partly documented entry, do not fill the missing steps by assuming that a nearby example covers
them. For an entry marked "not provided", read the reason; absence of a book answer is different from a
documented limitation of the code.

For example, when searching resource directories, `find_resource` returns the first candidate it can open
for reading and throws if no candidate can be opened ({{< code src/utils/find_resource.cpp find_resource >}}).
That source fact alone is not a complete answer to how a user should configure resource lookup. An answering
section must supply the relevant setup and conditions as well. This example is source reading, not an executed
resource-lookup test or a task classified as answered.

The map covers the original 32 questions and the supplemental spacing task. Four original questions
remain excluded from the paired 28-question comparison: Shomate, binary diffusion, molecular-diffusion
configuration and radiation/photochemistry coupling. Their presence here does not change that denominator.
The last three have routes elsewhere in the expanded book; Shomate retains an explicit scope statement.

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The statuses preserve a conservative distinction between available sections and complete answers.
Partly documented entries have not passed a new lookup round. In particular, species and saturation-law
extension procedures, mixture-capacity lookup, device/dtype contracts and GPU benchmarking still need
verification against their complete question. The spacing task links to its local definition; it does not
fill the shared notation group. Follow the destination's limits and tests before using its procedure.
:::
